channel.title: Pier & Point · UCSF Student Housing
channel.description: Changes, corrections and dated milestones for UCSF Student Housing (Mission Bay), San Francisco. Every item names its source.

item.title: Correction · UCSF Student Housing: The four UCSF Block 20 housing buildings showed an October 2005 opening that was only ever a 2002 forecast. Their completion now rests on SFGate's May 2009 report that the campus had four residential buildings, so they were complete by then; the actual opening date is still not confirmed.
item.description: The four UCSF Block 20 housing buildings showed an October 2005 opening that was only ever a 2002 forecast. Source: https://www.sfgate.com/health/article/135-million-UCSF-cancer-research-site-to-open-3229463.php.

item.title: Correction · UCSF Student Housing: The record no longer says the building opened around 2005 or in June 2005: no source read gives an opening date (Langan gives none and UCSF's housing page could not be read), so the milestone now carries the October 2005 full occupancy that the November 2002 Regents item anticipated, marked expected. The Regents approval is described as the committees approving and forwarding to the Board. Use now reads student, postdoctoral scholar and family housing (Langan, Regents) instead of student and faculty, the facts about the four-building complex cite Langan, the example of a parcel spanning several UCSF buildings now says about 12.2 acres at 675 Mission Bay Blvd, the SOM architect attribution cites arcCA Digest, and the aerial photo's caption no longer says 'from a departing flight'.

item.title: Added · UCSF Student Housing: The November 2002 UC Regents budget of $112,816,000 covers the whole Block 20 project (Hearst Tower plus the Housing North, Housing West and Student Housing buildings) with no per-building breakdown, so it is not a cost for Student Housing alone. It is now listed once in the shared site-wide cost list for Mission Bay, and this record points to it.

item.title: Complete · UCSF Student Housing: SFGate reports that, with the Helen Diller building's opening, the Mission Bay campus 'now has four research buildings, a community center and four residential buildings', so the Block 20 housing complex this building belongs to was complete by May 2009; no source read gives the date it actually opened (the November 2002 Regents item had anticipated full occupancy by October 2005) (~2009)

item.title: Planned · UCSF Student Housing: UC Regents' Grounds and Buildings and Finance committees approve, and vote to present to the Board, a $112,816,000 budget and external financing for the Mission Bay Block 20 Housing and Retail Project -- one 15-story tower and three mid-rise buildings around a shared courtyard, 298,800 residential asf and 430 apartment units total -- with construction to begin June 2003 and full occupancy anticipated by October 2005 (Nov 13, 2002)
item.description: UC Regents' Grounds and Buildings and Finance committees approve, and vote to present to the Board, a $112,816,000 budget and external financing for the Mission Bay Block 20 Housing and Retail Project -- one 15-story tower and three mid-rise buildings around a shared courtyard, 298,800 residential asf and 430 apartment units total -- with construction to begin June 2003 and full occupancy anticipated by October 2005 (Nov 13, 2002). Source: The Regents of the University of California, 2002-11.
